questions.question:
“The driver applied the _______ as soon as she approached the hotel where she wanted to take a _______.”

The words that best fill the blanks in the above sentence are
questions.explanation:
Verbal Aptitude → Vocabulary

Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given: A sentence with two blanks: "The driver applied the ___ as soon as she approached the hotel where she wanted to take a ___."
  • Find: The correct pair of homophones to fill the blanks.
  • Concepts used: Contextual vocabulary and homophones.

Solution

  • The first blank requires a noun referring to the mechanical device used to stop a vehicle. The correct spelling is "brake".
  • The second blank requires a noun referring to a pause or rest period. The correct spelling is "break".
  • Matching these definitions gives the sequence: brake, break.

Final Answer

Answer: brake, break
Correct option: (A)

questions.question:
For the given orthogonal matrix Q,
\[Q = \begin{bmatrix} 3/7 & 2/7 & 6/7 \\ -6/7 & 3/7 & 2/7 \\ 2/7 & 6/7 & -3/7 \end{bmatrix} \]
The inverse is
questions.explanation:
Linear Algebra (Matrices) | Orthogonal Matrices

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension
  • Given Data: Orthogonal matrix \(\mathbf{Q}\) where \(\mathbf{Q}^{-1} = \mathbf{Q}^T\)
  • Aim: Find \(\mathbf{Q}^{-1}\).

3. Core Concepts:

Orthogonal Matrix Property: For an orthogonal matrix, the inverse equals the transpose (rows become columns):

\[\mathbf{Q}^{-1} = \mathbf{Q}^T \]

Given:

\[\mathbf{Q} = \begin{bmatrix} 3/7 & 2/7 & 6/7 \\ -6/7 & 3/7 & 2/7 \\ 2/7 & 6/7 & -3/7 \end{bmatrix} \]

4. Solution Method:

Simply transpose \(\mathbf{Q}\) — convert rows to columns.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Original Matrix \(\mathbf{Q}\):

Column 1Column 2Column 3
Row 1\(3/7\)\(2/7\)\(6/7\)
Row 2\(-6/7\)\(3/7\)\(2/7\)
Row 3\(2/7\)\(6/7\)\(-3/7\)

Transpose \(\mathbf{Q}^T\) (Rows ↔ Columns):

Column 1Column 2Column 3
Row 1\(3/7\)\(-6/7\)\(2/7\)
Row 2\(2/7\)\(3/7\)\(6/7\)
Row 3\(6/7\)\(2/7\)\(-3/7\)

Verification of Orthogonality: Check \(\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{Q}^T = \mathbf{I}\)

  • Row 1 · Row 1: \((3/7)^2 + (2/7)^2 + (6/7)^2 = (9+4+36)/49 = 1\) ✓
  • Row 1 · Row 2: \((3/7)(-6/7) + (2/7)(3/7) + (6/7)(2/7) = (-18+6+12)/49 = 0\) ✓

6. Final Answer:

\[\mathbf{Q}^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} 3/7 & -6/7 & 2/7 \\ 2/7 & 3/7 & 6/7 \\ 6/7 & 2/7 & -3/7 \end{bmatrix} \]

Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | GA Q3
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: At the point \( x = 0 \), the function \( f(x) = x^3 \) has
options: neither local maximum nor local minimum

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: neither local maximum nor local minimum
structuredOptions.html: neither local maximum nor local minimum

questions.explanation:
Calculus (Differential Calculus) | Critical Points & Extrema

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: \(f(x) = x^3\) at \(x = 0\)
  • Aim: Determine the nature of the critical point at \(x = 0\).

3. Core Concepts:

First Derivative Test: \(f'(x) = 0\) gives a critical point. A sign change in \(f'(x)\) determines max/min.

Second Derivative Test:

  • \(f''(x) > 0\) → Local minimum
  • \(f''(x) < 0\) → Local maximum
  • \(f''(x) = 0\) → Test fails (point of inflection possible)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Find \(f'(x)\) and locate critical points.
  2. Apply higher-order derivative test when \(f''(x) = 0\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: First Derivative\[f'(x) = 3x^2 \]At \(x = 0\): \(f'(0) = 0\) → Critical point confirmed.
  2. Step 2: Second Derivative\[f''(x) = 6x \]At \(x = 0\): \(f''(0) = 0\) → Test inconclusive!
  3. Step 3: Higher-Order Test (Third Derivative)\[f'''(x) = 6 \neq 0 \]Since the first non-zero derivative is of odd order (3rd), \(x = 0\) is a point of inflection, not an extremum.
  4. Step 4: Sign Analysis of \(f'(x)\)
    Interval\(x\)\(f'(x) = 3x^2\)Sign
    \(x < 0\)\(-1\)\(3(1) = 3\)+
    \(x > 0\)\(+1\)\(3(1) = 3\)+

    \(f'(x) > 0\) on both sides → No sign change → No local max or min.

    Graphical Insight: \(f(x) = x^3\) is strictly increasing everywhere with a horizontal tangent at the origin (inflection point).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Neither local maximum nor local minimum | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | GA Q4
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: A column of height \( h \) with a rectangular cross-section of size \( a \times 2a \) has a buckling load of \( P \). If the cross-section is changed to \( 0.5a \times 3a \) and its height changed to \( 1.5h \), the buckling load of the redesigned column will be
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis (Stability) | Euler Buckling of Columns

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application (Proportionality analysis)
  • Given Data:
    • Original: Cross-section \(a \times 2a\), Height \(h\), Buckling load \(P\)
    • Redesigned: Cross-section \(0.5a \times 3a\), Height \(1.5h\)
  • Aim: Find new buckling load in terms of \(P\).

3. Core Concepts:

Euler Buckling Load:

\[P_{cr} = \dfrac{\pi^2 E I_{min}}{L_{eff}^2} \implies P_{cr} \propto \dfrac{I_{min}}{h^2} \]

Moment of Inertia for Rectangle:

  • About major axis: \(I_{xx} = \dfrac{bd^3}{12}\)
  • About minor axis: \(I_{yy} = \dfrac{db^3}{12}\)

For buckling, \(I_{min}\) governs (column buckles about the weaker axis).

4. Solution Method:

Calculate \(I_{min}\) for both configurations and apply proportionality.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Original Column (\(b_1 = a,\ d_1 = 2a,\ h_1 = h\)):

ParameterValue
\(I_{xx,1}\)\(\dfrac{a(2a)^3}{12} = \dfrac{2a^4}{3}\)
\(I_{yy,1}\) (Minimum ✓)\(\dfrac{2a \cdot a^3}{12} = \dfrac{a^4}{6}\)
\[P = \dfrac{\pi^2 E \cdot \dfrac{a^4}{6}}{h^2} = \dfrac{\pi^2 E a^4}{6h^2} \]

Redesigned Column (\(b_2 = 0.5a,\ d_2 = 3a,\ h_2 = 1.5h\)):

ParameterValue
\(I_{xx,2}\)\(\dfrac{0.5a \cdot (3a)^3}{12} = \dfrac{9a^4}{8}\)
\(I_{yy,2}\) (Minimum ✓)\(\dfrac{3a \cdot (0.5a)^3}{12} = \dfrac{a^4}{32}\)
\[P_{new} = \dfrac{\pi^2 E \cdot \dfrac{a^4}{32}}{(1.5h)^2} = \dfrac{\pi^2 E a^4}{32 \times 2.25 h^2} = \dfrac{\pi^2 E a^4}{72h^2} \]

Ratio Calculation:

\[\dfrac{P_{new}}{P} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\pi^2 E a^4}{72h^2}}{\dfrac{\pi^2 E a^4}{6h^2}} = \dfrac{6}{72} = \dfrac{1}{12} \]\[P_{new} = \dfrac{P}{12} \]

Sanity Check:

  • \(I_{min}\) ratio: \(\dfrac{a^4/32}{a^4/6} = \dfrac{6}{32} = \dfrac{3}{16}\)
  • Height factor: \((1.5)^2 = 2.25\)
  • Combined: \(\dfrac{3/16}{2.25} = \dfrac{3}{36} = \dfrac{1}{12}\) ✓

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(P/12\) | Correct option: (A)

questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question: A steel column of ISHB 350 @72.4 kg/m is subjected to a factored axial compressive load of 2000 kN. The load is transferred to a concrete pedestal of grade M20 through a square base plate. Consider bearing strength of concrete as \( 0.45f_{ck} \), where \( f_{ck} \) is the characteristic strength of concrete. Using limit state method and neglecting the self weight of base plate and steel column, the length of a side of the base plate to be provided is
questions.explanation:
Structural Engineering | Design of Steel Structures — Column Base Plate (IS 800:2007)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Factored axial load: \(P_u = 2000 \text{ kN}\)
    • Concrete grade: M20 (\(f_{ck} = 20 \text{ MPa}\))
    • Bearing strength \(= 0.45 f_{ck}\)
    • Square base plate; neglect self-weight of plate & column
  • Aim: Find the side length of the square base plate.

3. Core Concepts:

Bearing pressure on the concrete pedestal must not exceed \(0.45 f_{ck}\) (IS 800:2007 Clause 7.4.1). Uniform pressure is assumed under limit state.

\[A_{\text{req}} = \dfrac{P_u}{0.45 f_{ck}} \]

Note: \(1 \text{ MPa} = 10^3 \text{ kN/m}^2\) — consistent unit conversion is essential.

4. Solution Method:

Direct area calculation → side length \(= \sqrt{A}\). Choose the next higher standard size.

Common pitfall: Forgetting unit conversion (kN vs MPa) or including column self-weight (explicitly neglected).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Bearing Strength\[0.45 \times 20 = 9 \text{ MPa} = 9 \times 10^3 \text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  2. Step 2: Required Area\[A = \dfrac{2000}{9 \times 10^3} = 0.2222 \text{ m}^2 \]
  3. Step 3: Side Length\[L = \sqrt{0.2222} = 0.4714 \text{ m} = 47.14 \text{ cm} \]
  4. Step 4: Rounding up to the nearest practical size: 48 cm.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 48 cm | Correct option: (D)

questions.question: The Le Chatelier apparatus is used to determine
questions.explanation:
Materials Engineering | Cement Testing (IS 4031)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Le Chatelier apparatus
  • Aim: Identify what property it determines.

3. Core Concepts:

The Le Chatelier test measures expansion due to free lime/magnesia, thereby determining the soundness of cement.

  • IS 4031 (Part 3): Soundness by Le Chatelier → maximum permissible expansion = 10 mm.
  • Other tests: Vicat apparatus → setting time; Blaine apparatus → fineness; cube moulds → compressive strength.

4. Solution Method:

Direct recall of standard cement test apparatus-to-purpose mapping. No calculation required.

Pitfall: Confusing with Vicat (uses needles for consistency/setting) or Blaine (air permeability for fineness).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Recall: Le Chatelier mould = split cylinder with indicator pointers.
  2. Purpose: Detects unsoundness — excessive expansion after boiling.
  3. Eliminate others: Compressive → cube moulds; Fineness → Blaine; Setting → Vicat.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Soundness of cement | Correct option: (D)

questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question: The deformation in concrete due to sustained loading is
questions.explanation:
Concrete Technology | Properties of Hardened Concrete (IS 456:2000)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Deformation in concrete due to sustained loading.
  • Aim: Identify the phenomenon.

3. Core Concepts:

Creep = time-dependent deformation under constant sustained stress (IS 456 Clause 6.2.5).

  • Shrinkage: Volume reduction due to drying — load-independent.
  • Hydration: Chemical reaction between cement and water.
  • Segregation: Separation of constituents in fresh concrete.

The creep coefficient \(\theta\) is used in long-term deflection calculations per IS 456.

4. Solution Method:

Keyword matching: sustained loading → creep (not shrinkage, which is load-independent).

Pitfall: Mixing creep and shrinkage — both are long-term phenomena but have different causes.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Sustained load is present → eliminates shrinkage and hydration.
  2. Concrete under constant stress → viscoelastic (time-dependent) behaviour → creep.
  3. IS 456 confirms: long-term deformation under sustained loading = creep.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Creep | Correct option: (A)

2. Problem Analysis:

    • Two identical under-reinforced rectangular sections X and Y.
    • Section Y has 10% more longitudinal compression reinforcement: \(A_{sc,Y} = 1.1\, A_{sc,X}\).
    • Same \(A_{st}\), \(b\), \(d\), and material grades for both sections.

3. Core Concepts:

Under-reinforced sections: Tension steel yields before concrete crushes.

Equilibrium:

\[T = 0.87 f_y A_{st} = 0.36 f_{ck}\, b\, x_u + (f_{sc} - f_{cc})\, A_{sc} \]
  • Increasing \(A_{sc}\) → \(x_u\) decreases (less concrete compression needed to maintain equilibrium).
  • Moment increases due to additional compression steel couple: \(M_u = M_{u,\text{conc}} + A_{sc}(f_{sc})(d - d')\).
  • Ductility: Smaller \(x_u/d\) → higher ultimate curvature (\(\phi_u \propto 1/x_u\)) → more ductile.

4. Solution Method:

Compare the effect of extra \(A_{sc}\) on \(x_u\), \(M_u\), and ductility.

Pitfall: Assuming compression steel does not affect strength — it does via the additional moment couple.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Section X (less \(A_{sc}\)): larger \(x_u\) required to balance the same \(T\) → higher \(x_u/d\).
  2. Section Y (more \(A_{sc}\)): smaller \(x_u\), additional \(M_u\) from compression steel couple → higher \(M_u\).
  3. Smaller \(x_u\) in Y → higher ultimate curvature → Y is more ductile.
  4. Conclusion: Section X has lower flexural strength and is less ductile than Section Y.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Section X has less flexural strength and is less ductile than section Y | Correct option: (A)

questions.question: The percent reduction in the bearing capacity of a strip footing resting on sand under flooding condition (water level at the base of the footing) when compared to the situation where the water level is at a depth much greater than the width of footing, is approximately
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Bearing Capacity of Shallow Foundations (IS 6403 / Terzaghi)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension + Application
  • Given Data:
    • Strip footing on sand (\(c = 0\))
    • Case 1: Water table at the base of the footing
    • Case 2: Water table much deeper than \(B\) (no effect)
  • Aim: Percentage reduction in bearing capacity due to flooding (WT rising to base).

3. Core Concepts:

Terzaghi's bearing capacity (\(c = 0\)):

\[q_{ult} = 0.5\,\gamma\, B\, N_\gamma + \gamma\, D_f\, N_q \]

When the water table is at the base of the footing:

  • The \(0.5\gamma B N_\gamma\) term uses submerged unit weight \(\gamma' \approx \gamma/2\).
  • The surcharge term \(\gamma D_f N_q\) also uses \(\gamma'\) if water is at the base.
  • Both terms are approximately halved → \(q_{ult} \approx 50\%\) of the dry case.

Note: A 25% reduction applies when WT is at depth \(D_f/2\) below the base — a common pitfall.

4. Solution Method:

Compare \(\gamma\) vs \(\gamma'\) in both Terzaghi terms.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Dry case: Full \(\gamma\) in both terms.
  2. Submerged case (WT at base): Replace \(\gamma\) with \(\gamma' \approx \gamma/2\) in both terms.
  3. Ratio: \(q_{ult,\text{wet}} / q_{ult,\text{dry}} \approx 0.5\)
  4. Reduction \(= (1 - 0.5) \times 100\% = 50\%\)

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 50% | Correct option: (C)

questions.explanation:

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Aim: Identify the fluid properties and flow conditions for which Bernoulli's equation is applicable.

3. Core Concepts:

Bernoulli's Equation is derived from conservation of energy applied to fluid flow. Its standard assumptions are:

  • Fluid is inviscid (frictionless, \(\mu = 0\))
  • Fluid is incompressible (\(\rho = \text{constant}\))
  • Flow is steady (\(\partial v / \partial t = 0\))
  • Applied along a streamline

4. Solution Method:

Evaluate each option against these standard assumptions.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  • Option (A): Viscous and compressible — Incorrect. Viscosity causes energy losses not accounted for in the standard form.
  • Option (B): Inviscid and compressible — Incorrect. Standard form assumes constant (incompressible) density.
  • Option (C): Inviscid and incompressible — Correct. Matches the standard ideal fluid flow assumptions.
  • Option (D): Viscous and incompressible — Incorrect. Viscous flow requires an energy loss term: \(\dfrac{P_1}{\gamma} + \dfrac{v_1^2}{2g} + z_1 = \dfrac{P_2}{\gamma} + \dfrac{v_2^2}{2g} + z_2 + h_L\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Inviscid and incompressible fluid flow | Correct option: (C)

questions.question: A flow field is given by \( u = y^2 \), \( v = -xy \), \( w = 0 \). Value of the z-component of the angular velocity (in radians per unit time, up to two decimal places) at the point \( (0, -1, 1) \) is _______
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Kinematics of Flow: Angular Velocity

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Velocity field: \(u = y^2, v = -xy, w = 0\)
    Point of interest: \((0, -1, 1)\)
  • Aim: Determine z-component of angular velocity \(\omega_z\) (rad/unit time)

3. Core Concepts:

  • Angular velocity vector \(\vec{\omega} = \dfrac{1}{2}(\nabla \times \vec{V})\)
  • Z-component formula: \(\omega_z = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial x} - \dfrac{\partial u}{\partial y}\right)\)
  • Standard assumption: Flow is continuous and differentiable

4. Solution Method:

  • Compute partial derivatives of velocity components
  • Substitute into angular velocity formula
  • Evaluate at given coordinates
  • Pitfall Alert: Sign convention in curl operation; remember the \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) factor

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Compute partial derivatives:
    \[\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial x} = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(-xy) = -y \]
    \[\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial y} = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(y^2) = 2y \]
  2. Apply angular velocity formula:
    \[ \omega_z = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial x} - \dfrac{\partial u}{\partial y}\right] = \dfrac{1}{2}[-y - 2y] = \dfrac{1}{2}(-3y) = -\dfrac{3y}{2} \]
  3. Evaluate at point \((0, -1, 1)\) where \(y = -1\):
    \[\omega_z = -\dfrac{3(-1)}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2} = 1.50 \text{ rad/unit time} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer(for NAT): \(1.50\) rad/unit time | Accepted range: 1.50 to 1.50

questions.question: In a fillet weld, the direct shear stress and bending tensile stress are 50 MPa and 150 MPa, respectively. As per IS 800: 2007, the equivalent stress (in MPa, up to two decimal places) will be _______

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q20
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: In a shrinkage limit test, the volume and mass of a dry soil pat are found to be 50 cm³ and 88 g, respectively. The specific gravity of the soil solids is 2.71 and the density of water is 1 g/cc. The shrinkage limit (in %, up to two decimal places) is _______
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shrinkage Limit Determination

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Dry soil pat volume \(V_d = 50 \text{ cm}^3\)
    Dry soil pat mass \(M_d = 88 \text{ g}\)
    Specific gravity \(G = 2.71\)
    Water density \(\rho_w = 1 \text{ g/cm}^3\)
  • Aim: Calculate shrinkage limit \(w_s\) (%)

3. Core Concepts:

  • Shrinkage limit: Water content at transition from semi-solid to solid state
  • Formula derivation: At shrinkage limit, soil is saturated with volume \(V_d\)
    \[ w_s = \left[\dfrac{(V_d - V_s)\rho_w}{M_d}\right] \times 100\% \]
    where \(V_s = \dfrac{M_d}{G\rho_w}\) = volume of solids
  • IS 2720 (Part 6):1972 governs shrinkage limit test procedures

4. Solution Method:

  • Compute volume of solids \(V_s\)
  • Determine volume of water at shrinkage limit: \(V_w = V_d - V_s\)
  • Convert to mass of water and compute water content
  • Sanity Check: Typical shrinkage limits for clays: 10-30%; result must be positive and < liquid limit

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate volume of solids \(V_s\):
    \[V_s = \dfrac{M_d}{G \cdot \rho_w} = \dfrac{88 \text{ g}}{2.71 \times 1 \text{ g/cm}^3} = 32.4723 \text{ cm}^3 \]
  2. Calculate volume of water at shrinkage limit:
    \[V_w = V_d - V_s = 50 - 32.4723 = 17.5277 \text{ cm}^3 \]
  3. Mass of water (since \(\rho_w = 1 \text{ g/cm}^3\)):
    \[M_w = 17.5277 \text{ g} \]
  4. Compute shrinkage limit:
    \[w_s = \dfrac{M_w}{M_d} \times 100\% = \dfrac{17.5277}{88} \times 100\% = 19.918\% \approx 19.92\% \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer(for NAT): \(19.92\)% | Accepted range: 19.50 to 20.50

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q22
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A 1:50 model of a spillway is to be tested in the laboratory. The discharge in the prototype spillway is 1000 m³/s. The corresponding discharge (in m³/s, up to two decimal places) to be maintained in the model, neglecting variation in acceleration due to gravity, is _______
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Hydraulic Similitude: Froude Scaling

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Scale ratio (model:prototype) \(L_r = 1:50\)
    Prototype discharge \(Q_p = 1000 \text{ m}^3/\text{s}\)
    Gravity variation neglected (\(g_m = g_p\))
  • Aim: Determine model discharge \(Q_m\) (m³/s)

3. Core Concepts:

  • Froude number similarity for free-surface flows: \(Fr_m = Fr_p\)
  • Discharge scale ratio derivation:
    \[\dfrac{Q_m}{Q_p} = \left(\dfrac{L_m}{L_p}\right)^{5/2} = L_r^{5/2} \]
  • Key assumption: Spillway flow is gravity-dominated; viscous/surface tension effects negligible

4. Solution Method:

  • Apply Froude scaling law for discharge
  • Compute \(L_r^{5/2}\) carefully
  • Pitfall Alert: Exponent is 5/2 (not 2 or 3); ensure model:prototype ratio direction is correct

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Establish scale ratio:
    \[L_r = \dfrac{L_m}{L_p} = \dfrac{1}{50} \]
  2. Apply discharge scaling law:
    \[\dfrac{Q_m}{Q_p} = L_r^{5/2} = \left(\dfrac{1}{50}\right)^{5/2} = \dfrac{1}{50^{2.5}} \]
  3. Compute \(50^{2.5}\):
    \[50^{2.5} = 50^2 \times 50^{0.5} = 2500 \times \sqrt{50} = 2500 \times 7.07107 = 17677.67 \]
  4. Calculate model discharge:
    \[Q_m = Q_p \times \dfrac{1}{17677.67} = \dfrac{1000}{17677.67} = 0.05657 \text{ m}^3/\text{s} \]
  5. Round to two decimals:
    \[Q_m \approx 0.06 \text{ m}^3/\text{s} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer(for NAT): \(0.06\) m³/s | Accepted range: 0.05 to 0.06

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q23

questions.question: A 10 m wide rectangular channel carries a discharge of 20 m³/s under critical condition. Using \( g = 9.81 \text{ m/s}^2 \), the specific energy (in m, up to two decimal places) is _______
questions.explanation:
Open Channel Flow | Critical Flow & Specific Energy

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Rectangular channel width \(B = 10 \text{ m}\)
    Discharge \(Q = 20 \text{ m}^3/\text{s}\)
    Critical flow condition
    \(g = 9.81 \text{ m/s}^2\)
  • Aim: Calculate specific energy \(E\) at critical flow (m)

3. Core Concepts:

  • Unit discharge: \(q = Q/B\)
  • Critical depth for rectangular channel: \(y_c = \left(\dfrac{q^2}{g}\right)^{1/3}\)
  • Specific energy at critical flow: \(E_c = y_c + \dfrac{V_c^2}{2g} = \dfrac{3}{2}y_c\) (key simplification)
  • Fundamental principle: At critical flow, Froude number \(Fr = 1\)

4. Solution Method:

  • Compute unit discharge \(q\)
  • Calculate critical depth \(y_c\)
  • Apply \(E_c = 1.5y_c\) relationship
  • Alternative: Compute \(V_c = q/y_c\) then \(E_c = y_c + V_c^2/(2g)\) for verification

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate unit discharge:
    \[q = \dfrac{Q}{B} = \dfrac{20}{10} = 2 \text{ m}^2/\text{s} \]
  2. Compute critical depth \(y_c\):
    \[y_c = \left(\dfrac{q^2}{g}\right)^{1/3} = \left(\dfrac{2^2}{9.81}\right)^{1/3} = \left(\dfrac{4}{9.81}\right)^{1/3} = (0.407747)^{1/3} \]
    \[y_c = 0.7415 \text{ m} \]
  3. Apply specific energy formula for critical flow:
    \[E_c = \dfrac{3}{2}y_c = 1.5 \times 0.7415 = 1.1123 \text{ m} \]
  4. Round to two decimals:
    \[E_c \approx 1.11 \text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer(for NAT): \(1.11\) m | Accepted range: 1.10 to 1.20

questions.question: For routing of flood in a given channel using the Muskingum method, two of the routing coefficients are estimated as \( C_0 = -0.25 \) and \( C_1 = 0.55 \). The value of the third coefficient \( C_2 \) would be _______

  • Muskingum routing equation: \(O_2 = C_0I_2 + C_1I_1 + C_2O_1\)
  • Fundamental constraint: Coefficients must sum to unity for mass conservation
    \[C_0 + C_1 + C_2 = 1 \]
  • Derived from continuity equation and storage-discharge relationship \(S = K[xI + (1-x)O]\)

4. Solution Method:

  • Apply coefficient summation constraint
  • Solve algebraically for \(C_2\)
  • Sanity Check: Coefficients should typically satisfy \(0 \leq C_1, C_2 \leq 1\); \(C_0\) can be negative for certain \(x\) values

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Apply mass conservation constraint:
    \[C_0 + C_1 + C_2 = 1 \]
  2. Substitute known values:
    \[-0.25 + 0.55 + C_2 = 1 \]
  3. Solve for \(C_2\):
    \[0.30 + C_2 = 1 \quad \Rightarrow \quad C_2 = 1 - 0.30 = 0.70 \]

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q25

questions.question: A city generates \( 40 \times 10^6 \) kg of municipal solid waste (MSW) per year, out of which only 10% is recovered/recycled and the rest goes to landfill. The landfill has a single lift of 3 m height and is compacted to a density of 550 kg/m³. If 80% of the landfill is assumed to be MSW, the landfill area (in m², up to one decimal place) required would be _______
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Landfill Design & Waste Management

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Annual MSW generation: \(40 \times 10^6 \text{ kg}\)
    Recovery rate: 10% → Landfill fraction: 90%
    Landfill lift height \(H = 3 \text{ m}\)
    Compacted landfill density \(\rho_{\text{landfill}} = 550 \text{ kg/m}^3\)
    MSW occupies 80% of total landfill volume
  • Aim: Calculate required landfill area (m²)

3. Core Concepts:

  • Mass-volume-density relationship: \(V = M/\rho\)
  • Volume allocation: MSW volume is fraction of total landfill volume
  • Area calculation: \(A = V_{\text{total}}/H\)
  • Standard practice: Account for cover material, gas vents, liner systems in volume allocation

4. Solution Method:

  • Calculate mass of MSW to landfill
  • Convert to compacted MSW volume
  • Account for 80% MSW occupancy to find total landfill volume
  • Divide by lift height for area
  • Unit discipline: kg → m³ via density; ensure consistent SI units throughout

  1. Calculate MSW mass to landfill:
    \[M_{\text{landfill}} = 40 \times 10^6 \text{ kg} \times (1 - 0.10) = 36 \times 10^6 \text{ kg} \]
  2. Calculate volume of compacted MSW:
    \[V_{\text{MSW}} = \dfrac{M_{\text{landfill}}}{\rho_{\text{landfill}}} = \dfrac{36 \times 10^6 \text{ kg}}{550 \text{ kg/m}^3} = 65454.545 \text{ m}^3 \]

    \[V_{\text{total}} = \dfrac{V_{\text{MSW}}}{0.80} = \dfrac{65454.545}{0.80} = 81818.182 \text{ m}^3 \]

    \[A = \dfrac{V_{\text{total}}}{H} = \dfrac{81818.182 \text{ m}^3}{3 \text{ m}} = 27272.727 \text{ m}^2 \]

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q26
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The value of the integral \(\displaystyle \int_0^{\pi} x \cos^2 x \, dx \) is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Integral Calculus

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Definite integral: \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi} x \cos^2 x \, dx\)
  • Aim: Evaluate the exact value of the given definite integral.

3. Core Concepts:

Property of Definite Integrals (King's Rule):

\[\int_{0}^{a} f(x) \, dx = \int_{0}^{a} f(a - x) \, dx \]

This property is exceptionally useful for removing the algebraic multiplier \(x\) from trigonometric integrands.

Trigonometric Identities:

\(\cos(\pi - \theta) = -\cos\theta \implies \cos^2(\pi - \theta) = \cos^2\theta\)

\(\cos^2 x = \dfrac{1 + \cos(2x)}{2}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Let the given integral be \(I\).
  2. Apply the King's Rule to substitute \(x\) with \((\pi - x)\).
  3. Add the original integral and the new integral. The variable \(x\) will cancel out, leaving a simpler trigonometric integral multiplied by \(\pi\).
  4. Use the double-angle identity for \(\cos^2 x\) to evaluate the resulting integral.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Define the integral.\[I = \int_{0}^{\pi} x \cos^2 x \, dx \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)} \]
  2. Step 2: Apply the property \(\displaystyle \int_{0}^{a} f(x) \, dx = \int_{0}^{a} f(a - x) \, dx\).\[I = \int_{0}^{\pi} (\pi - x) \cos^2(\pi - x) \, dx \]Since \(\cos(\pi - x) = -\cos x\), squaring gives \(\cos^2 x\).\[I = \int_{0}^{\pi} (\pi - x) \cos^2 x \, dx \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)} \]
  3. Step 3: Add Equation 1 and Equation 2.\[I + I = \int_{0}^{\pi} x \cos^2 x \, dx + \int_{0}^{\pi} (\pi - x) \cos^2 x \, dx \]\[2I = \int_{0}^{\pi} (x + \pi - x) \cos^2 x \, dx \]\[2I = \pi \int_{0}^{\pi} \cos^2 x \, dx \]
  4. Step 4: Substitute the trigonometric identity for \(\cos^2 x\).\[2I = \pi \int_{0}^{\pi} \left( \dfrac{1 + \cos 2x}{2} \right) dx \]\[ 2I = \dfrac{\pi}{2} \left[x + \dfrac{\sin 2x}{2} \right]_{0}^{\pi} \]
  5. Step 5: Evaluate the limits.\[ 2I = \dfrac{\pi}{2} \left[\left(\pi + \dfrac{\sin 2\pi}{2}\right) - \left(0 + \dfrac{\sin 0}{2}\right) \right] \]Knowing that \(\sin 2\pi = 0\) and \(\sin 0 = 0\):\[ 2I = \dfrac{\pi}{2} [\pi + 0 - 0 - 0] \]\[2I = \dfrac{\pi^2}{2} \implies I = \dfrac{\pi^2}{4} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\dfrac{\pi^2}{4}\) | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q27
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question: A cantilever beam of length 2 m with a square section of side length 0.1 m is loaded vertically at the free end. The vertical displacement at the free end is 5 mm. The beam is made of steel with Young’s modulus of \( 2.0 \times 10^{11} \text{ N/m}^2 \). The maximum bending stress at the fixed end of the cantilever is
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Bending Stresses & Deflection of Beams

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Beam type: Cantilever, loaded vertically at free end (Point Load \(P\))
    • Span Length: \(L = 2 \text{ m}\)
    • Cross-section: Square with side \(a = 0.1 \text{ m}\)
    • Vertical displacement at free end: \(\Delta = 5 \text{ mm} = 0.005 \text{ m}\)
    • Young's Modulus: \(E = 2.0 \times 10^{11} \text{ N/m}^2\)
  • Aim: Calculate the maximum bending stress (\(\sigma_{max}\)) at the fixed end.

3. Core Concepts:

Deflection of Cantilever Beam: For a point load \(P\) at the free end, maximum deflection is \(\Delta = \dfrac{PL^3}{3EI}\)

Bending Equation (Euler-Bernoulli): \(\dfrac{M}{I} = \dfrac{\sigma}{y} = \dfrac{E}{R}\)

Maximum Bending Moment: Occurs at the fixed support, \(M_{max} = P \times L\)

Maximum Bending Stress: \(\sigma_{max} = \dfrac{M_{max}}{Z}\), where Section Modulus \(Z = \dfrac{I}{y_{max}}\)

Properties of Square Section: Moment of Inertia \(I = \dfrac{a^4}{12}\), Extreme fiber distance \(y_{max} = \dfrac{a}{2}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Since load \(P\) is unknown, use the given deflection \(\Delta\) to calculate \(P\) indirectly.
  2. Formulate the equation for maximum bending moment \(M\) using \(P\).
  3. Substitute \(M\) into the bending stress formula.

Alternative shortcut: A direct relationship between deflection and stress can be derived: \(\sigma_{max} = \dfrac{3E \Delta y_{max}}{L^2}\), bypassing the calculation of \(P\) and \(I\) altogether.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Calculate geometric properties of the cross-section.
    \[I = \dfrac{b d^3}{12} = \dfrac{(0.1)(0.1)^3}{12} = \dfrac{10^{-4}}{12} \text{ m}^4 \]\[y_{max} = \dfrac{d}{2} = \dfrac{0.1}{2} = 0.05 \text{ m} \]\[Z = \dfrac{I}{y_{max}} = \dfrac{10^{-4}/12}{0.05} = \dfrac{10^{-4}}{0.6} = 1.6667 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^3 \]
  2. Step 2: Calculate the applied load \(P\) from deflection.\[\Delta = \dfrac{PL^3}{3EI} \]\[0.005 = \dfrac{P \times (2)^3}{3 \times (2.0 \times 10^{11}) \times \left(\dfrac{10^{-4}}{12}\right)} \]\[0.005 = \dfrac{8P}{5 \times 10^6} \]\[P = \dfrac{0.005 \times 5 \times 10^6}{8} = \dfrac{25000}{8} = 3125 \text{ N} \]
  3. Step 3: Calculate the maximum bending moment \(M\).
    The maximum bending moment occurs at the fixed end:\[M = P \times L = 3125 \text{ N} \times 2 \text{ m} = 6250 \text{ N·m} \]
  4. Step 4: Calculate maximum bending stress.\[\sigma_{max} = \dfrac{M}{Z} = \dfrac{6250}{1.6667 \times 10^{-4}} = 6250 \times 6000 = 37{,}500{,}000 \text{ N/m}^2 \]
  5. Step 5: Unit conversion to MPa.
    Since \(1 \text{ MPa} = 10^6 \text{ N/m}^2\),\[\sigma_{max} = 37.5 \text{ MPa} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 37.5 MPa | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q28
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
A cylinder of radius 250 mm and weight, W = 10 kN is rolled up an obstacle of height 50 mm by applying a horizontal force P at its centre as shown in the figure.



All interfaces are assumed frictionless. The minimum value of P is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mechanics | Equilibrium & Statics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Radius of cylinder: \(R = 250 \text{ mm}\)
    • Weight of cylinder: \(W = 10 \text{ kN}\) (acting vertically downwards through the center)
    • Obstacle height: \(h = 50 \text{ mm}\)
    • Horizontal force \(P\) applied at the center
  • Aim: Find the minimum value of \(P\) required to roll the cylinder up the obstacle.

3. Core Concepts:

Impending Motion / Verge of Rolling: When the cylinder is just about to roll over the obstacle, it loses contact with the ground. The normal reaction from the horizontal floor becomes zero.

Pivot Point: The entire cylinder pivots around the corner/tip of the obstacle.

Moment Equilibrium (\(\sum M = 0\)): For equilibrium at the verge of rolling, the overturning moment caused by force \(P\) must exactly equal the restoring moment caused by the self-weight \(W\) about the pivot point.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Identify the pivot point (Point \(A\), the top corner of the obstacle).
  2. Establish the lever arms for both forces \(P\) and \(W\) with respect to Point \(A\) using geometry.
  3. Apply \(\sum M_A = 0\) to find the unknown force \(P\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Geometric setup of lever arms.
    Let \(O\) be the center of the cylinder. Force \(P\) acts horizontally through \(O\). Force \(W\) acts vertically through \(O\). The pivot point \(A\) is at a height \(h = 50 \text{ mm}\) from the ground.

    Vertical distance from \(O\) to \(A\) (Lever arm for \(P\)):
    Let this be \(y\). Since \(O\) is at height \(R = 250 \text{ mm}\) from the ground,\[y = R - h = 250 - 50 = 200 \text{ mm} \]Horizontal distance from \(O\) to \(A\) (Lever arm for \(W\)):
    Let this be \(x\). In the right-angled triangle formed by \(O\), \(A\), and the horizontal line through \(A\), the hypotenuse is the radius \(R\).\[x^2 + y^2 = R^2 \]\[x = \sqrt{R^2 - y^2} = \sqrt{250^2 - 200^2} \]\[x = \sqrt{62500 - 40000} = \sqrt{22500} = 150 \text{ mm} \]
  2. Step 2: Apply Moment Equilibrium Equation.
    Take moments about the pivot point \(A\):
    • Overturning moment due to \(P\): Clockwise moment \(= P \times y\)
    • Restoring moment due to \(W\): Anti-clockwise moment \(= W \times x\)
    For minimum \(P\) to initiate rolling:\[P \times y = W \times x \]\[P \times 200 = 10 \text{ kN} \times 150 \]
  3. Step 3: Solve for \(P\).\[P = 10 \times \dfrac{150}{200} \]\[P = 10 \times 0.75 = 7.5 \text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 7.5 kN | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q29
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
A plate in equilibrium is subjected to uniform stresses along its edges with magnitude \( \sigma_{xx} = 30 \text{ MPa} \) and \( \sigma_{yy} = 50 \text{ MPa} \) as shown in the figure.



The Young’s modulus of the material is \( 2 \times 10^{11} \text{ N/m}^2 \) and the Poisson’s ratio is 0.3. If \( \sigma_{zz} \) is negligibly small and assumed to be zero, then the strain \( \varepsilon_{zz} \) is
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Stress-Strain Relationships

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Stress in X-direction: \(\sigma_{xx} = 30 ext{ MPa}\) (Tension, positive)
    • Stress in Y-direction: \(\sigma_{yy} = 50 ext{ MPa}\) (Tension, positive)
    • Stress in Z-direction: \(\sigma_{zz} = 0 ext{ MPa}\) (Plane stress condition on Z-face)
    • Young's Modulus: \(E = 2 imes 10^{11} ext{ N/m}^2 = 200{,}000 ext{ MPa}\)
    • Poisson's Ratio: \( u = 0.3\)
  • Aim: Calculate the normal strain in the Z-direction (\(\varepsilon_{zz}\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Generalized Hooke's Law: The strain in any direction is caused by the direct stress in that direction minus the lateral Poisson's effect from stresses in orthogonal directions.

Formula for 3D Strain:\[\varepsilon_{zz} = \dfrac{\sigma_{zz}}{E} - \dfrac{ u \sigma_{xx}}{E} - \dfrac{ u \sigma_{yy}}{E} \]

Sign Convention: Tensile stresses are taken as positive (+), compressive stresses as negative (−).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Convert all parameters to a consistent unit system (MPa for stresses and modulus).
  2. Note that although \(\sigma_{zz} = 0\), the strain \(\varepsilon_{zz}\) is not zero due to the Poisson's effect of \(\sigma_{xx}\) and \(\sigma_{yy}\). This is known as transverse contraction.
  3. Substitute the values into the generalized Hooke's Law equation and compute the final strain.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Check and convert units.
    \(\sigma_{xx} = +30 ext{ MPa}\)
    \(\sigma_{yy} = +50 ext{ MPa}\)
    \(E = 2 imes 10^{11} ext{ N/m}^2 = 2 imes 10^5 ext{ N/mm}^2 = 200{,}000 ext{ MPa}\)
  2. Step 2: Apply Generalized Hooke's Law for Z-direction.\[ \varepsilon_{zz} = \dfrac{1}{E} [\sigma_{zz} - u(\sigma_{xx} + \sigma_{yy})] \]Since \(\sigma_{zz} = 0\):\[\varepsilon_{zz} = - \dfrac{ u}{E} (\sigma_{xx} + \sigma_{yy}) \]
  3. Step 3: Substitute values and calculate.\[\varepsilon_{zz} = - \dfrac{0.3}{200{,}000} (30 + 50) \]\[\varepsilon_{zz} = - \dfrac{0.3 imes 80}{200{,}000} \]\[\varepsilon_{zz} = - \dfrac{24}{200{,}000} \]\[\varepsilon_{zz} = -120 imes 10^{-6} \]

    Physical Insight: The negative sign indicates that the plate is contracting (thinning) in the Z-direction as a result of being stretched in both X and Y directions.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(-120 imes 10^{-6}\) | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q30
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
The figure shows a simply supported beam PQ of uniform flexural rigidity EI carrying two moments M and 2M.



The slope at P will be
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Deflection of Beams

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Simply supported beam PQ of total length \(L\) (\(L/3 + L/3 + L/3\))
    • Uniform flexural rigidity \(= EI\)
    • Two concentrated moments applied: \(M\) at \(L/3\) from P (clockwise) and \(2M\) at \(2L/3\) from P (clockwise)
  • Aim: Find the slope at the support P (\(\theta_P\)).

2. Core Concepts:

We use Macaulay's Method (Double Integration Method). The governing differential equation for beam deflection is:

\[EI \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -M_x \]

Sign convention: sagging moments are positive, hogging moments are negative.

3. Solution Method:

  1. Step 1: Determine the Support Reactions
    Taking moments about support Q (\(\sum M_Q = 0\)):\[R_P \times L - M - 2M = 0 \]\[R_P = \dfrac{3M}{L} \quad (\text{acting upwards}) \]
  2. Step 2: Formulate the Bending Moment Equation (\(M_x\))
    Taking a section at distance \(x\) from P, using Macaulay's brackets:\[M_x = \dfrac{3M}{L} x - M \langle x - L/3 \rangle^0 - 2M \langle x - 2L/3 \rangle^0 \]
  3. Step 3: Integrate to find Slope and Deflection
    Substituting into the governing equation:\[EI \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -\dfrac{3M}{L} x + M \langle x - L/3 \rangle^0 + 2M \langle x - 2L/3 \rangle^0 \]Integrating once for slope:\[EI \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{3M}{2L} x^2 + M \langle x - L/3 \rangle^1 + 2M \langle x - 2L/3 \rangle^1 + C_1 \]Integrating twice for deflection:\[EI\, y = -\dfrac{M}{2L} x^3 + \dfrac{M}{2} \langle x - L/3 \rangle^2 + M \langle x - 2L/3 \rangle^2 + C_1 x + C_2 \]
  4. Step 4: Apply Boundary Conditions
    At \(x = 0,\ y = 0 \implies C_2 = 0\)
    At \(x = L,\ y = 0\):\[0 = -\dfrac{ML^2}{2} + \dfrac{M}{2}\left(\dfrac{2L}{3}\right)^2 + M\left(\dfrac{L}{3}\right)^2 + C_1 L \]\[0 = -\dfrac{ML^2}{2} + \dfrac{2ML^2}{9} + \dfrac{ML^2}{9} + C_1 L \]\[0 = -\dfrac{ML^2}{2} + \dfrac{ML^2}{3} + C_1 L \]\[C_1 L = \dfrac{ML^2}{2} - \dfrac{ML^2}{3} = \dfrac{ML^2}{6} \implies C_1 = \dfrac{ML}{6} \]
  5. Step 5: Calculate Slope at P (\(x = 0\))\[EI \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)_{x=0} = C_1 = \dfrac{ML}{6} \]\[\theta_P = \dfrac{ML}{6EI} \]

4. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\dfrac{ML}{6EI}\) | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q31
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A 0.5 m × 0.5 m square concrete pile is to be driven in a homogeneous clayey soil having undrained shear strength, \( c_u = 50 \text{ kPa} \) and unit weight, \( \gamma = 18.0 \text{ kN/m}^3 \). The design capacity of the pile is 500 kN. The adhesion factor α is given as 0.75. The length of the pile required for the above design load with a factor of safety of 2.0 is
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Deep Foundations

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Pile dimensions: \(0.5 \text{ m} \times 0.5 \text{ m}\)
    • Undrained shear strength of clay: \(c_u = 50 \text{ kPa}\)
    • Adhesion factor: \(\alpha = 0.75\)
    • Design Capacity: \(Q_d = 500 \text{ kN}\)
    • Factor of Safety: \(FOS = 2.0\)
  • Aim: Find the required length of the pile (\(L\)).

2. Core Concepts:

For piles in cohesive soils (clay) under undrained conditions, ultimate load capacity (\(Q_u\)) is the sum of end bearing (\(Q_b\)) and skin friction (\(Q_s\)):

\[Q_u = Q_b + Q_s = (c_u \cdot N_c \cdot A_b) + (\alpha \cdot c_u \cdot A_s) \]
  • Skempton's bearing capacity factor for deep foundations: \(N_c = 9\)
  • End area: \(A_b = B \times B\)
  • Surface area: \(A_s = 4 \times B \times L\)
  • Ultimate Capacity: \(Q_u = Q_{design} \times FOS\)

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Calculate Target Ultimate Capacity\[Q_u = 500 \text{ kN} \times 2.0 = 1000 \text{ kN} \]
  2. Step 2: Calculate End Bearing Resistance (\(Q_b\))\[A_b = 0.5 \times 0.5 = 0.25 \text{ m}^2 \]\[Q_b = c_u \cdot N_c \cdot A_b = 50 \times 9 \times 0.25 = 112.5 \text{ kN} \]
  3. Step 3: Formulate Skin Friction Resistance (\(Q_s\))\[A_s = \text{Perimeter} \times L = (4 \times 0.5) \times L = 2L \text{ m}^2 \]\[Q_s = \alpha \cdot c_u \cdot A_s = 0.75 \times 50 \times 2L = 75L \text{ kN} \]
  4. Step 4: Solve for L\[Q_u = Q_b + Q_s \]\[1000 = 112.5 + 75L \]\[75L = 887.5 \]\[L = \dfrac{887.5}{75} = 11.833 \text{ m} \]

4. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 11.8 m | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q32
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A closed tank contains 0.5 m thick layer of mercury (specific gravity = 13.6) at the bottom. A 2.0 m thick layer of water lies above the mercury layer. A 3.0 m thick layer of oil (specific gravity = 0.6) lies above the water layer. The space above the oil layer contains air under pressure. The gauge pressure at the bottom of the tank is 196.2 kN/m². The density of water is 1000 kg/m³ and the acceleration due to gravity is 9.81 m/s². The value of pressure in the air space is
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Hydrostatics

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Mercury layer: \(h_{Hg} = 0.5 \text{ m}\), Specific Gravity \(S_{Hg} = 13.6\)
    • Water layer: \(h_w = 2.0 \text{ m}\), Specific Gravity \(S_w = 1.0\)
    • Oil layer: \(h_{oil} = 3.0 \text{ m}\), Specific Gravity \(S_{oil} = 0.6\)
    • Unit weight of water: \(\gamma_w = 9.81 \text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Gauge pressure at bottom: \(P_{bottom} = 196.2 \text{ kN/m}^2\)
  • Aim: Find the gauge pressure of the air space (\(P_{air}\)).

2. Core Concepts:

Using the Hydrostatic Law, the pressure at the bottom of the tank is the sum of the air pressure and the pressures exerted by each fluid column:

\[P_{bottom} = P_{air} + P_{oil} + P_{water} + P_{Hg} \]\[P = \gamma \cdot h = (S \cdot \gamma_w) \cdot h \]

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Calculate hydrostatic pressures of liquids\[P_{oil} = (0.6 \times 9.81) \times 3.0 = 17.658 \text{ kN/m}^2 \]\[P_{water} = (1.0 \times 9.81) \times 2.0 = 19.62 \text{ kN/m}^2 \]\[P_{Hg} = (13.6 \times 9.81) \times 0.5 = 66.708 \text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  2. Step 2: Setup Equation and Solve\[P_{bottom} = P_{air} + P_{oil} + P_{water} + P_{Hg} \]\[196.2 = P_{air} + 17.658 + 19.62 + 66.708 \]\[196.2 = P_{air} + 103.986 \]\[P_{air} = 196.2 - 103.986 = 92.214 \text{ kN/m}^2 \]

4. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 92.214 kN/m² | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q33
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: A rapid sand filter comprising a number of filter beds is required to produce 99 MLD of potable water. Consider water loss during backwashing as 5%, rate of filtration as 6.0 m/h and length to width ratio of filter bed as 1.35. The width of each filter bed is to be kept equal to 5.2 m. One additional filter bed is to be provided to take care of break-down, repair and maintenance. The total number of filter beds required will be
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Water Treatment

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Net filtered output required: \(99 \text{ MLD}\)
    • Water loss during backwashing: \(5\%\)
    • Rate of filtration: \(V_f = 6.0 \text{ m/h}\)
    • Width of filter bed: \(B = 5.2 \text{ m}\)
    • Length/Width ratio: \(L/B = 1.35\)
    • Standby units: 1 (for breakdown/maintenance)
  • Aim: Find the total number of filter beds required.

2. Core Concepts:

Total Flow Calculation: Because 5% of the gross filtered water is lost in backwashing, the 99 MLD output represents 95% of the total water filtered.

\[Q_{gross} = \dfrac{Q_{net}}{1 - \text{loss fraction}} \]

Required Area: \(\text{Total Area} = \dfrac{Q_{gross}}{V_f}\)

Number of operational units: \(N_{op} = \dfrac{\text{Total Area required}}{\text{Area of one bed}}\)

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Determine Gross Filtered Water Requirement\[Q_{gross} = \dfrac{99}{0.95} = 104.21 \text{ MLD} \]Convert to \(\text{m}^3/\text{h}\):\[Q_{gross} = \dfrac{104.21 \times 10^6}{1000 \times 24} = 4342.105 \text{ m}^3/\text{h} \]
  2. Step 2: Calculate Surface Area of One Filter Bed\[L = 1.35 \times B = 1.35 \times 5.2 = 7.02 \text{ m} \]\[\text{Area}_{bed} = 7.02 \times 5.2 = 36.504 \text{ m}^2 \]
  3. Step 3: Discharge Capacity of One Filter Bed\[Q_{bed} = 36.504 \times 6.0 = 219.024 \text{ m}^3/\text{h} \]
  4. Step 4: Number of Filter Beds\[N_{op} = \dfrac{4342.105}{219.024} = 19.82 \approx 20 \text{ (rounded up)} \]\[\text{Total Beds} = N_{op} + 1\text{ (Standby)} = 20 + 1 = 21 \text{ beds} \]

    Note: GATE accepted both 21 and 22. Some designers assume an additional bed is concurrently taken offline for routine backwashing alongside the general standby unit. By standard normative calculations, 21 is mathematically rigorous.

4. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 21 | Correct option: (C) (GATE Key: C or D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q34
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question: A priority intersection has a single-lane one-way traffic road crossing an undivided two-lane two-way traffic road. The traffic stream speed on the single-lane road is 20 kmph and the speed on the two-lane road is 50 kmph. The perception-reaction time is 2.5 s, coefficient of longitudinal friction is 0.38 and acceleration due to gravity is 9.81 m/s². A clear sight triangle has to be ensured at this intersection. The minimum lengths of the sides of the sight triangle along the two-lane road and the single-lane road, respectively will be
questions.explanation:
Transportation Engineering | Sight Distance at Intersections

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Priority intersection (Uncontrolled/Yield/Stop behavior for minor road)
    • Major road: 2-lane, 2-way, \(v_{major} = 50 \text{ kmph}\)
    • Minor road: single-lane, 1-way, \(v_{minor} = 20 \text{ kmph}\)
    • Also given (red herrings): \(t_r = 2.5 \text{ s}\), \(f = 0.38\)
  • Aim: Minimum lengths of sight triangle sides along major and minor roads.

2. Core Concepts:

Common Pitfall: Many students will calculate the Stopping Sight Distance (SSD) for both roads using \(v t_r + v^2/2gf\), which yields ~61 m and 18 m (Option B). This formula is exclusively for uncontrolled intersections.

Code Reference (IRC:66-1976 — Sight Distance at Intersections): For a priority intersection (one road clearly designated as major), the crossing driver on the minor road must wait for a safe gap:

  • The minor road distance is fixed strictly at 15 meters (distance from the major road edge where the driver stops to observe).
  • The sight distance along the major road is the distance traveled by a vehicle at design speed over an 8-second time gap.

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Sight Triangle leg along the Minor Road
    Based on IRC:66 provision for priority intersections:\[d_{minor} = 15 \text{ m} \]
  2. Step 2: Sight Triangle leg along the Major Road
    Convert major road speed to m/s:\[v_{major} = 50 \times \dfrac{5}{18} = 13.889 \text{ m/s} \]Using the 8-second rule:\[d_{major} = 13.889 \times 8 = 111.11 \approx 111 \text{ m} \]

4. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 111 m and 15 m | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q35
questions.subject: Surveying & Geomatics
questions.question:
The following details refer to a closed traverse:

LineConsecutive coordinate
Northing (m)Southing (m)Easting (m)Westing (m)
PQ----437173----
QR101----558----
RS419--------96
SP----83----634


The length and direction (whole circle bearing) of closure, respectively are
questions.explanation:
Geomatics | Traverse Computations

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: 4-leg closed traverse with Northing/Southing (Latitudes) and Easting/Westing (Departures).
  • Aim: Determine the length and direction (WCB) of closure.

2. Core Concepts:

  • Latitude (\(\Delta N\) / \(\Sigma L\)): Northing is Positive (+), Southing is Negative (−).
  • Departure (\(\Delta E\) / \(\Sigma D\)): Easting is Positive (+), Westing is Negative (−).
  • The Error of Closure vector (\(e\)) describes how much the traverse misses the origin.
  • The Correction / Closing Line vector is exactly equal and opposite to the error.

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Sum the Latitudes (\(\Sigma L\))\[\Sigma L = \text{Northings} - \text{Southings} \]\[\Sigma L = (101 + 419) - (437 + 83) = 520 - 520 = 0 \text{ m} \]
  2. Step 2: Sum the Departures (\(\Sigma D\))\[\Sigma D = \text{Eastings} - \text{Westings} \]\[\Sigma D = (173 + 558) - (96 + 634) = 731 - 730 = +1 \text{ m (Easting)} \]
  3. Step 3: Determine Length of Closure\[\text{Length} = \sqrt{(\Sigma L)^2 + (\Sigma D)^2} = \sqrt{0^2 + 1^2} = 1 \text{ m} \]
  4. Step 4: Determine Direction of Closure
    • Error Vector: \(0\text{ m North},\ 1\text{ m East} \implies\) Azimuth \(= 90^\circ\) (Due East)
    • Closing (Correction) Vector: Opposite direction \(\implies 0\text{ m North},\ 1\text{ m West} \implies\) Azimuth \(= 270^\circ\) (Due West)

    Both 90° and 270° are technically justifiable depending on whether the examiner implies 'Closure Error' or 'Closing Correction Line'. Standard key accepted both.

4. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1 m and 90° (or 1 m and 270°) | Correct option: (A) or (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q36
questions.subject: Surveying & Geomatics
questions.question: A square area (on the surface of the earth) with side 100 m and uniform height, appears as 1 cm² on a vertical aerial photograph. The topographic map shows that a contour of 650 m passes through the area. If focal length of the camera lens is 150 mm, the height from which the aerial photograph was taken, is
questions.explanation:
Geomatics | Photogrammetry

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Area of square on ground: \(100 \text{ m} \times 100 \text{ m} = 10{,}000 \text{ m}^2\)
    • Area on aerial photograph: \(1 \text{ cm}^2\)
    • Elevation of terrain: \(h = 650 \text{ m}\)
    • Camera focal length: \(f = 150 \text{ mm} = 0.15 \text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Height from which the photograph was taken (\(H\)) above Mean Sea Level.

2. Core Concepts:

Linear Scale (\(S\)): Ratio of distance on the map to distance on the ground.

\[S = \dfrac{f}{H - h} \]

Areal Scale (\(S^2\)): Square of the linear scale.

\[S^2 = \dfrac{\text{Area on Photograph}}{\text{Area on Ground}} \]

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Determine the Areal Scale
    Convert photograph area to SI units:\[A_{photo} = 1 \text{ cm}^2 = 1 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2 \]\[A_{ground} = 10{,}000 \text{ m}^2 = 10^4 \text{ m}^2 \]\[S^2 = \dfrac{1 \times 10^{-4}}{10^4} = 10^{-8} \]
  2. Step 2: Determine the Linear Scale (\(S\))\[S = \sqrt{10^{-8}} = 10^{-4} = \dfrac{1}{10{,}000} \]
  3. Step 3: Calculate the Flying Height (\(H\))
    Using \(S = \dfrac{f}{H - h}\):\[\dfrac{1}{10{,}000} = \dfrac{0.15}{H - 650} \]\[H - 650 = 0.15 \times 10{,}000 = 1500 \]\[H = 1500 + 650 = 2150 \text{ m} \]

4. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2150 m | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q37
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The solution at \( x = 1, t = 1 \) of the partial differential equation \( \dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} = 25 \dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} \) subject to initial conditions of \( u(0) = 3x \) and \( \dfrac{\partial u}{\partial t}(0) = 3 \) is _______
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Partial Differential Equations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • PDE: \(\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} = 25 \dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}\)
    • Initial displacement: \(u(x,0) = 3x\)
    • Initial velocity: \(\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial t}(x,0) = 3\)
  • Aim: Find the value of \(u(x,t)\) at \(x = 1,\ t = 1\).

3. Core Concepts:

1D Wave Equation: The standard form is \(\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}\).

D'Alembert's Solution: For an infinite string with initial displacement \(f(x)\) and initial velocity \(g(x)\):

\[ u(x,t) = \dfrac{1}{2}[f(x-ct) + f(x+ct)] + \dfrac{1}{2c} \int_{x-ct}^{x+ct} g(s)\, ds \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Rearrange the given PDE to standard form to find the wave speed \(c\).
  2. Identify the functions \(f(x)\) and \(g(x)\) from the initial conditions.
  3. Substitute \(x=1,\ t=1\) and compute the function values and the integral.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Determine wave speed \(c\)
    Given: \(\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} = 25\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} \implies \dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} = \dfrac{1}{25}\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}\)
    Comparing with standard form: \(c^2 = \dfrac{1}{25} \implies c = \dfrac{1}{5}\)
  2. Step 2: Identify initial conditions
    \(f(x) = u(x,0) = 3x\)
    \(g(x) = \dfrac{\partial u}{\partial t}(x,0) = 3\)
  3. Step 3: Apply D'Alembert's Equation at \(x=1,\ t=1\)\[ u(1,1) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[f\!\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right) + f\!\left(\dfrac{6}{5}\right)\right] + \dfrac{5}{2}\int_{4/5}^{6/5} 3\, ds \]
  4. Step 4: Evaluate each term
    Displacement part:
    \(f(4/5) = 3(4/5) = 12/5\)
    \(f(6/5) = 3(6/5) = 18/5\)\[ \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{12}{5} + \dfrac{18}{5}\right] = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 6 = 3 \]Velocity part:\[ \dfrac{5}{2}[3s]_{4/5}^{6/5} = \dfrac{15}{2}\left(\dfrac{6}{5} - \dfrac{4}{5}\right) = \dfrac{15}{2} \times \dfrac{2}{5} = 3 \]
  5. Step 5: Final sum\[u(1,1) = 3 + 3 = 6 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 6 | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q38
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The solution (up to three decimal places) at \( x = 1 \) of the differential equation \( \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 2\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 0 \) subject to boundary conditions \( y(0) = 1 \) and \( \dfrac{dy}{dx}(0) = -1 \) is _______
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Ordinary Differential Equations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • ODE: \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 2\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 0\)
    • Boundary Conditions: \(y(0) = 1\) and \(y'(0) = -1\)
  • Aim: Find the solution \(y(1)\) up to three decimal places.

3. Core Concepts:

Linear Homogeneous 2nd Order ODEs: Solved by finding the roots of the characteristic (auxiliary) equation \(am^2 + bm + c = 0\).

Repeated Roots: If roots \(m_1 = m_2 = m\), the general solution is: \(y(x) = (C_1 + C_2 x)e^{mx}\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Write the characteristic equation and find its roots.
  2. Form the general solution \(y(x)\).
  3. Use \(y(0) = 1\) to find \(C_1\).
  4. Differentiate \(y(x)\) and use \(y'(0) = -1\) to find \(C_2\).
  5. Evaluate the particular solution at \(x = 1\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Characteristic Equation\[m^2 + 2m + 1 = 0 \implies (m+1)^2 = 0 \implies m = -1,\ -1 \]
  2. Step 2: General Solution\[y(x) = (C_1 + C_2 x)e^{-x} \]
  3. Step 3: Apply \(y(0) = 1\)\[y(0) = (C_1 + 0)e^0 = C_1 \implies C_1 = 1 \]
  4. Step 4: Apply \(y'(0) = -1\)
    Differentiating using the product rule:\[y'(x) = C_2 e^{-x} - (C_1 + C_2 x)e^{-x} \]Substituting \(x=0,\ C_1=1\):\[y'(0) = C_2 - 1 = -1 \implies C_2 = 0 \]
  5. Step 5: Particular solution evaluated at \(x=1\)
    With \(C_1 = 1,\ C_2 = 0\):\[y(x) = e^{-x} \]\[y(1) = e^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{e} \approx 0.367879 \approx 0.368 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.368 | Accepted key range: 0.36 to 0.37

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q39
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Variation of water depth (y) in a gradually varied open channel flow is given by the first order differential equation

\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1 - e^{-\frac{10}{3}\ln(y)}}{250 - 45e^{-3\ln(y)}} \]

Given initial condition: \( y(x = 0) = 0.8 \text{ m} \). The depth (in m, up to three decimal places) of flow at a downstream section at \( x = 1 \text{ m} \) from one calculation step of Single Step Euler Method is _______
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Numerical Methods

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • ODE: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1 - e^{-\dfrac{10}{3}\ln(y)}}{250 - 45e^{-3\ln(y)}}\)
    • Initial condition: \(y(0) = 0.8 \text{ m}\)
    • Step size: \(h = 1\) m (one calculation step from \(x=0\) to \(x=1\))
  • Aim: Find \(y(1)\) using the Single Step Euler Method.

3. Core Concepts:

Euler's Forward Method:

\[y_{i+1} = y_i + h \cdot f(x_i, y_i) \]

Logarithmic Identity: \(e^{k\ln(y)} = y^k\). This simplifies the expression significantly.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Simplify \(f(x,y)\) using logarithmic properties.
  2. Evaluate the slope \(f(x_0, y_0)\) at \(x_0 = 0,\ y_0 = 0.8\).
  3. Apply Euler's formula to find \(y_1\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Simplify \(f(x,y)\)\[f(x,y) = \dfrac{1 - y^{-10/3}}{250 - 45y^{-3}} \]
  2. Step 2: Evaluate at \(y_0 = 0.8\)
    Numerator component: \((0.8)^{-10/3} = (1.25)^{10/3} \approx 2.10444\)
    Denominator component: \((0.8)^{-3} = (1.25)^3 = 1.953125\)\[f(0,\ 0.8) = \dfrac{1 - 2.10444}{250 - 45 \times 1.953125} = \dfrac{-1.10444}{250 - 87.8906} = \dfrac{-1.10444}{162.109} \approx -0.006813 \]
  3. Step 3: Euler's Method step\[y(1) = 0.8 + 1 \times (-0.006813) = 0.793187 \approx 0.793 \text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.793 | Accepted key range: 0.78 to 0.80

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q40
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question: An RCC short column (with lateral ties) of rectangular cross section of 250 mm × 300 mm is reinforced with four numbers of 16 mm diameter longitudinal bars. The grades of steel and concrete are Fe415 and M20, respectively. Neglect eccentricity effect. Considering limit state of collapse in compression (IS 456 : 2000), the axial load carrying capacity of the column (in kN, up to one decimal place), is _______
questions.explanation:
RCC Design | Limit State of Collapse: Compression

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Cross section: \(b = 250 \text{ mm},\ D = 300 \text{ mm}\)
    • Reinforcement: 4 bars of 16 mm diameter
    • Materials: Fe415 (\(f_y = 415 \text{ MPa}\)), M20 (\(f_{ck} = 20 \text{ MPa}\))
    • Constraint: Neglect eccentricity effect
  • Aim: Find the axial load carrying capacity (\(P_u\)) in kN.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Area of Steel (\(A_{sc}\)): Cross-sectional area of longitudinal bars.
  • Area of Concrete (\(A_c\)): Gross area (\(A_g\)) minus area of steel (\(A_{sc}\)).
  • Standard Code Formula (IS 456 Cl 39.3): \(P_u = 0.4 f_{ck}A_c + 0.67 f_y A_{sc}\) — accounts for minimum accidental eccentricity up to \(0.05D\).
  • Pure Axial Formula (when eccentricity is explicitly neglected): \(P_0 = 0.45 f_{ck}A_c + 0.75 f_y A_{sc}\).

Note: GATE accepted both interpretations. The pure axial formula is used here as the problem explicitly states to neglect eccentricity.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate \(A_g\) and \(A_{sc}\).
  2. Deduct \(A_{sc}\) from \(A_g\) to find \(A_c\).
  3. Substitute into the pure axial load capacity equation.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Calculate Areas\[A_g = 250 \times 300 = 75{,}000 \text{ mm}^2 \]\[A_{sc} = 4 \times \dfrac{\pi}{4} \times (16)^2 = 4 \times 201.06 = 804.25 \text{ mm}^2 \]\[A_c = 75{,}000 - 804.25 = 74{,}195.75 \text{ mm}^2 \]
  2. Step 2: Apply Capacity Formula (Neglecting Eccentricity)\[P_0 = 0.45 f_{ck} A_c + 0.75 f_y A_{sc} \]\[P_0 = 0.45(20)(74{,}195.75) + 0.75(415)(804.25) \]\[P_0 = 667{,}761.75 \text{ N} + 250{,}322.81 \text{ N} \]\[P_0 = 918{,}084.56 \text{ N} \approx 918.1 \text{ kN} \]

    Using the standard code formula \(P_u = 0.4f_{ck}A_c + 0.67f_yA_{sc}\) gives 817.2 kN. Both interpretations were rewarded.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 918.1 kN | Accepted key range: 815 to 830 OR 905 to 920

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q41
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Limit State Design of Beams & Slabs
questions.question: An RCC beam of rectangular cross section has factored shear of 200 kN at its critical section. Its width b is 250 mm and effective depth d is 350 mm. Assume design shear strength \( \tau_c \) of concrete as 0.62 N/mm² and maximum allowable shear stress \( \tau_{c,max} \) in concrete as 2.8 N/mm². If two legged 10 mm diameter vertical stirrups of Fe250 grade steel are used, then the required spacing (in cm, up to one decimal place) as per limit state method will be _______
questions.explanation:
RCC Design | Limit State of Collapse: Shear

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • \(b = 250 \text{ mm},\ d = 350 \text{ mm}\)
    • Factored Shear: \(V_u = 200 \text{ kN} = 200{,}000 \text{ N}\)
    • \(\tau_c = 0.62 \text{ N/mm}^2\)
    • \(\tau_{c,max} = 2.8 \text{ N/mm}^2\)
    • Stirrups: 2-legged, 10 mm dia, Fe250 steel (\(f_y = 250 \text{ MPa}\))
  • Aim: Find the required spacing \(s_v\) in cm.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Nominal Shear Stress: \(\tau_v = \dfrac{V_u}{bd}\) (Must be \(< \tau_{c,max}\) to prevent diagonal compression failure)
  • Shear Resisted by Concrete: \(V_c = \tau_c b d\)
  • Shear Resisted by Stirrups: \(V_{us} = V_u - V_c\)
  • Spacing of Vertical Stirrups (IS 456 Cl 40.4): \(s_v = \dfrac{0.87 f_y A_{sv} d}{V_{us}}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Verify section is safe in diagonal compression.
  2. Determine required shear reinforcement force (\(V_{us}\)).
  3. Calculate area of stirrup legs (\(A_{sv}\)).
  4. Calculate required spacing (\(s_v\)) in mm, then convert to cm.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Verify Section Safety\[\tau_v = \dfrac{200 \times 1000}{250 \times 350} = 2.286 \text{ N/mm}^2 \]Since \(\tau_v\ (2.286) < \tau_{c,max}\ (2.8)\), the section is safe.
  2. Step 2: Force Components\[V_c = 0.62 \times 250 \times 350 = 54{,}250 \text{ N} = 54.25 \text{ kN} \]\[V_{us} = 200 - 54.25 = 145.75 \text{ kN} = 145{,}750 \text{ N} \]
  3. Step 3: Stirrup Properties
    For 2-legged 10 mm dia stirrup:\[A_{sv} = 2 \times \dfrac{\pi}{4} \times (10)^2 = 157.08 \text{ mm}^2 \]
  4. Step 4: Required Spacing\[s_v = \dfrac{0.87 \times 250 \times 157.08 \times 350}{145{,}750} = \dfrac{11{,}957{,}715}{145{,}750} \approx 82.04 \text{ mm} \]Unit Conversion:\[s_v = 82.04 \text{ mm} = 8.204 \text{ cm} \approx 8.2 \text{ cm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 8.2 cm | Accepted key range: 7.0 to 9.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q42
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question:
The dimensions of a symmetrical welded I-section are shown in the figure.



The plastic section modulus about the weaker axis (in cm³, up to one decimal place) is _______
questions.explanation:
Steel Structures | Plastic Analysis

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Symmetrical I-section
    • Flange width: \(b_f = 140 \text{ mm}\), Flange thickness: \(t_f = 9 \text{ mm}\)
    • Web depth: \(d_w = 200 \text{ mm}\), Web thickness: \(t_w = 6.1 \text{ mm}\)
  • Aim: Find the plastic section modulus (\(Z_p\)) about the weaker axis in cm³.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Weaker Axis: For a standard I-section, the weaker axis is the vertical axis (\(y\text{-}y\)) passing through the center of the web.
  • Plastic Neutral Axis (PNA): Due to symmetry about the \(y\text{-}y\) axis, the PNA coincides with the geometric centroidal axis, splitting the total area equally.
  • Plastic Section Modulus:\[Z_p = \sum A_i |\bar{x}_i| = 2 \times (\text{First moment of area of one half about PNA}) \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Split the section vertically down the center of the web.
  2. Identify elements on one half: half-top flange, half-bottom flange, and half-web.
  3. Compute the area and centroid distance for each half-element.
  4. Sum the moments of area, double it, and convert to cm³.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Elements of the right-half section

    Top Flange (right half):
    Width \(= 140/2 = 70 \text{ mm}\)
    \(A_{f1} = 70 \times 9 = 630 \text{ mm}^2\)
    \(\bar{x}_{f1} = 70/2 = 35 \text{ mm}\)

    Bottom Flange (right half):
    \(A_{f2} = 630 \text{ mm}^2,\ \bar{x}_{f2} = 35 \text{ mm}\)

    Web (right half):
    Thickness \(= 6.1/2 = 3.05 \text{ mm}\)
    \(A_w = 200 \times 3.05 = 610 \text{ mm}^2\)
    \(\bar{x}_w = 3.05/2 = 1.525 \text{ mm}\)
  2. Step 2: Compute \(Z_{py}\)\[ Z_{py} = 2 \times [(A_{f1}\bar{x}_{f1}) + (A_{f2}\bar{x}_{f2}) + (A_w\bar{x}_w)] \]\[ Z_{py} = 2 \times [(630 \times 35) + (630 \times 35) + (610 \times 1.525)] \]\[ Z_{py} = 2 \times [22{,}050 + 22{,}050 + 930.25] \]\[Z_{py} = 2 \times 45{,}030.25 = 90{,}060.5 \text{ mm}^3 \]
  3. Step 3: Unit Conversion\[Z_{py} = \dfrac{90{,}060.5}{10^3} = 90.06 \text{ cm}^3 \approx 90.1 \text{ cm}^3 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 90.1 cm³ | Accepted key range: 88.0 to 92.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q43
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
Consider the deformable pin-jointed truss with loading, geometry and section properties as shown in the figure.



Given that \( E = 2 \times 10^{11} \text{ N/m}^2 \), \( A = 10 \text{ mm}^2 \), \( L = 1 \text{ m} \) and \( P = 1 \text{ kN} \). The horizontal displacement of Joint C (in mm, up to one decimal place) is _______
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Deflection of Trusses

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Modulus of Elasticity: \(E = 2 \times 10^{11} \text{ N/m}^2\)
    • Reference Area: \(A = 10 \text{ mm}^2 = 10 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^2\)
    • Length parameter: \(L = 1 \text{ m}\)
    • External Loads: \(P = 1 \text{ kN}\) (horizontal rightwards), \(2P = 2 \text{ kN}\) (vertical downwards)
    • Cross-sectional areas: Member AC \(= 2A\), Member BC \(= A\), Member AB \(= A\)
  • Aim: Find the horizontal displacement of Joint C (\(\Delta_{Cx}\)) in mm.

3. Core Concepts:

Support Identification: Joint A is a roller (restricts vertically, free horizontally) and Joint B is a pin (restricts both translations).

Virtual Work Method (Unit Load Method):

\[\Delta = \sum \dfrac{N \cdot n \cdot L_{member}}{A_{member} \cdot E} \]

where \(N\) = member force due to real loads, \(n\) = member force due to a virtual unit load at the desired joint in the desired direction.

Common Pitfall: Misidentifying the supports (e.g., treating A as a pin and B as a roller) will make \(N_{AB} = 0\), leading to an incorrect deflection of 2.2 mm, outside the correct range.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Find real support reactions recognizing A as a roller and B as a pin.
  2. Use method of joints to find real axial forces (\(N\)).
  3. Remove real loads, apply a 1 unit horizontal load rightwards at C, and find virtual forces (\(n\)).
  4. Tabulate and compute the sum for deflection.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Real Support Reactions
    Joints: A at \((0,0)\), B at \((L,0)\), C at \((L,L)\).\[\sum M_B = 0 \implies R_{Ay} \cdot L + P \cdot L = 0 \implies R_{Ay} = -P \text{ (downwards)} \]\[\sum F_y = 0 \implies -P + R_{By} - 2P = 0 \implies R_{By} = 3P \text{ (upwards)} \]\[\sum F_x = 0 \implies R_{Bx} + P = 0 \implies R_{Bx} = -P \text{ (leftwards)} \]
  2. Step 2: Real Member Forces (\(N\))
    Joint A:\[N_{AC} = P\sqrt{2} \text{ (Tension)}, \quad N_{AB} = -P \text{ (Compression)} \]Joint C:\[N_{BC} = -3P \text{ (Compression)} \]
  3. Step 3: Virtual Member Forces (\(n\))
    Apply 1 unit load rightwards at C, real loads zeroed.
    Virtual reactions: \(R'_{Ay} = -1,\ R'_{By} = 1,\ R'_{Bx} = -1\)
    \(n_{AC} = \sqrt{2}\), \(n_{AB} = -1\), \(n_{BC} = -1\)
  4. Step 4: Deflection Calculation
    Stiffness constant:\[\dfrac{PL}{AE} = \dfrac{1000 \text{ N} \times 1000 \text{ mm}}{10 \text{ mm}^2 \times 2 \times 10^5 \text{ N/mm}^2} = 0.5 \text{ mm} \]
    Member\(N\)\(n\)\(L_{mem}\)AreaContribution
    AC\(P\sqrt{2}\)\(\sqrt{2}\)\(L\sqrt{2}\)\(2A\)\(\sqrt{2} \times 0.5 = 0.707 \text{ mm}\)
    BC\(-3P\)\(-1\)\(L\)\(A\)\(3 \times 0.5 = 1.500 \text{ mm}\)
    AB\(-P\)\(-1\)\(L\)\(A\)\(1 \times 0.5 = 0.500 \text{ mm}\)
    \[\Delta_{Cx} = 0.707 + 1.500 + 0.500 = 2.707 \text{ mm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2.7 mm | Accepted key range: 2.60 to 2.80

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q44
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
At a construction site, a contractor plans to make an excavation as shown in the figure.



The water level in the adjacent river is at an elevation of +20.0 m. Unit weight of water is 10 kN/m³. The factor of safety (up to two decimal places) against sand boiling for the proposed excavation is _______
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Seepage and Earth Pressure

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Excavation base elevation: \(+10 \text{ m}\)
    • Sand layer top elevation: \(0 \text{ m}\)
    • Remaining clay layer thickness: \(H_{clay} = 10 \text{ m}\)
    • Clay unit weight: \(\gamma_{clay} = 20 \text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Unit weight of water: \(\gamma_w = 10 \text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Piezometric head in sand (river water level): \(+20 \text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Determine the Factor of Safety (FoS) against sand boiling at the excavation base.

3. Core Concepts:

Sand Boiling (Heave): Occurs when the upward pore water pressure in a pervious layer exceeds the downward total effective weight of the overlying confining soil plug.

\[FoS = \dfrac{\text{Total downward stress } (\sigma_v)}{\text{Upward pore water pressure } (u)} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Compute the total downward vertical stress \(\sigma_v\) at the clay-sand interface (Elevation 0).
  2. Determine the upward pore water pressure \(u\) exerted by the aquifer at Elevation 0.
  3. Divide downward stress by upward pore pressure.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Total Vertical Stress (\(\sigma_v\))\[\sigma_v = \gamma_{clay} \times H_{clay} = 20 \times 10 = 200 \text{ kPa} \]
  2. Step 2: Upward Pore Water Pressure (\(u\))
    The highly pervious sand is hydraulically connected to the river (water level \(+20 \text{ m}\)).
    Pressure head at Elevation 0: \(h_w = 20 - 0 = 20 \text{ m}\)\[u = \gamma_w \times h_w = 10 \times 20 = 200 \text{ kPa} \]
  3. Step 3: Factor of Safety\[FoS = \dfrac{\sigma_v}{u} = \dfrac{200}{200} = 1.00 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.00 | Accepted key range: 1.00 to 1.03

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q45
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A conventional drained triaxial compression test was conducted on a normally consolidated clay sample under an effective confining pressure of 200 kPa. The deviator stress at failure was found to be 400 kPa. An identical specimen of the same clay sample is isotropically consolidated to a confining pressure of 200 kPa and subjected to standard undrained triaxial compression test. If the deviator stress at failure is 150 kPa, the pore pressure developed (in kPa, up to one decimal place) is _______
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shear Strength of Soils

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • CD Test (NC Clay): Effective confining stress \(\sigma_3' = 200 \text{ kPa}\), Deviator stress \(\Delta\sigma_d = 400 \text{ kPa}\)
    • CU Test (same NC Clay): Confining stress \(\sigma_3 = 200 \text{ kPa}\), Deviator stress at failure \(\Delta\sigma_d = 150 \text{ kPa}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the pore water pressure \(u_f\) generated at failure in the CU test.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Normally Consolidated (NC) Clay: Effective cohesion intercept is zero (\(c' = 0\)).
  • Effective Stress Principle: \(\phi'\) is an intrinsic soil property, identical for CD and CU tests.
  • Failure Criterion for \(c' = 0\):\[\sin(\phi') = \dfrac{\sigma_1' - \sigma_3'}{\sigma_1' + \sigma_3'} \]
  • Undrained State: \(\sigma_1' = \sigma_1 - u_f\) and \(\sigma_3' = \sigma_3 - u_f\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Use CD test results to find \(\phi'\).
  2. Write total principal stresses at failure for the CU test.
  3. Express effective stresses parametrically using \(u_f\).
  4. Equate to the failure envelope and solve for \(u_f\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Determine \(\phi'\) from the CD test
    \(\sigma_3' = 200 \text{ kPa}\), \(\sigma_1' = 200 + 400 = 600 \text{ kPa}\)\[\sin(\phi') = \dfrac{600 - 200}{600 + 200} = \dfrac{400}{800} = 0.5 \implies \phi' = 30^\circ \]
  2. Step 2: Stresses for the CU test
    • Total: \(\sigma_3 = 200 \text{ kPa}\), \(\sigma_1 = 200 + 150 = 350 \text{ kPa}\)
    • Effective: \(\sigma_1' = 350 - u_f\), \(\sigma_3' = 200 - u_f\)
  3. Step 3: Solve for \(u_f\)
    Substituting \(\sin 30^\circ = 0.5\):\[0.5 = \dfrac{(350 - u_f) - (200 - u_f)}{(350 - u_f) + (200 - u_f)} = \dfrac{150}{550 - 2u_f} \]\[550 - 2u_f = 300 \implies 2u_f = 250 \implies u_f = 125 \text{ kPa} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 125.0 kPa | Accepted key range: 124 to 126

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q46
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The void ratio of a soil is 0.55 at an effective normal stress of 140 kPa. The compression index of the soil is 0.25. In order to reduce the void ratio to 0.4, an increase in the magnitude of effective normal stress (in kPa, up to one decimal place) should be _______
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Consolidation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Initial void ratio: \(e_1 = 0.55\)
    • Initial effective normal stress: \(\sigma_1' = 140 \text{ kPa}\)
    • Compression index: \(C_c = 0.25\)
    • Target final void ratio: \(e_2 = 0.4\)
  • Aim: Determine the required increase in effective normal stress (\(\Delta\sigma'\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Compression Index Equation: The fundamental relationship governing 1D primary consolidation:

\[\Delta e = e_1 - e_2 = C_c \log_{10}\!\left(\dfrac{\sigma_2'}{\sigma_1'}\right) \]

The actual stress increment applied is \(\Delta\sigma' = \sigma_2' - \sigma_1'\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the change in void ratio \(\Delta e\).
  2. Substitute into the consolidation equation to solve for final effective stress \(\sigma_2'\).
  3. Subtract \(\sigma_1'\) from \(\sigma_2'\) to find the stress increase.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Calculate Void Ratio Change\[\Delta e = 0.55 - 0.40 = 0.15 \]
  2. Step 2: Calculate Final Effective Stress (\(\sigma_2'\))\[0.15 = 0.25 \cdot \log_{10}\!\left(\dfrac{\sigma_2'}{140}\right) \]\[\log_{10}\!\left(\dfrac{\sigma_2'}{140}\right) = \dfrac{0.15}{0.25} = 0.6 \]\[\dfrac{\sigma_2'}{140} = 10^{0.6} \approx 3.98107 \]\[\sigma_2' = 140 \times 3.98107 = 557.35 \text{ kPa} \]
  3. Step 3: Required Stress Increase\[\Delta\sigma' = 557.35 - 140 = 417.35 \text{ kPa} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 417.4 kPa | Accepted key range: 416.0 to 420.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q47
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A rigid smooth retaining wall of height 7 m with vertical backface retains saturated clay as backfill. The saturated unit weight and undrained cohesion of the backfill are 17.2 kN/m³ and 20 kPa, respectively. The difference in the active lateral forces on the wall (in kN per meter length of wall, up to two decimal places), before and after the occurrence of tension cracks is _______
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Lateral Earth Pressure

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Wall height: \(H = 7 \text{ m}\)
    • Saturated unit weight: \(\gamma_{sat} = 17.2 \text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Undrained cohesion: \(c_u = 20 \text{ kPa}\)
  • Aim: Find the difference in active lateral forces (kN/m) before and after tension cracks develop.

3. Core Concepts:

Active Earth Pressure (Rankine): \(p_a = \gamma z K_a - 2c\sqrt{K_a}\)

Undrained Loading (\(\phi_u = 0\)): \(K_a = 1\), so \(p_a = \gamma z - 2c_u\)

Tension Zone: Negative pressure (tension) exists near the surface up to depth \(z_c = \dfrac{2c_u}{\gamma}\).

Before vs After Cracks:

  • Before cracks: Soil is intact — wall experiences both pull (negative) and push (positive) forces.
  • After cracks: Soil separates from wall — tensile force is lost; only push force acts.
  • Difference: Equals the gross magnitude of the lost negative (tension) force — the area of the tension triangle.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Compute tension crack depth \(z_c\).
  2. Compute the area of the negative (tension) pressure triangle.
  3. This area directly equals the change in total load on the wall upon cracking.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Tension Crack Depth\[z_c = \dfrac{2c_u}{\gamma_{sat}} = \dfrac{2 \times 20}{17.2} = 2.3256 \text{ m} \]
  2. Step 2: Earth Pressure at Surface (\(z = 0\))\[p_a = \gamma(0) - 2c_u = 0 - 2(20) = -40 \text{ kPa} \]
  3. Step 3: Difference in Active Force\[F_{diff} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times z_c \times |p_{a,z=0}| = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2.3256 \times 40 = 46.51 \text{ kN/m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 46.51 kN/m | Accepted key range: 45 to 49 (or −49 to −45)

questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
Rainfall depth over a watershed is monitored through six number of well distributed rain gauges. Gauged data are given below

The Thiessen mean value (in mm, up to one decimal place) of the rainfall is _______
questions.explanation:

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Six rain gauges with recorded rainfall depths \(P_i\) (mm) and Thiessen polygon areas \(A_i\) (\(\times 10^4 \text{ m}^2\)):
    Gauge\(P_i\) (mm)\(A_i\) (\(\times 10^4 \text{ m}^2\))

  • Aim: Calculate the Thiessen mean rainfall over the watershed (mm, to one decimal place).
