The Thiessen Polygon method assigns an area of influence to each rain gauge. The mean precipitation is the area-weighted average:

\[\bar{P} = \dfrac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} (P_i \times A_i)}{\sum_{i=1}^{n} A_i} \]

Note: Since all areas share the multiplier \(10^4 \text{ m}^2\), it cancels in numerator and denominator — raw integer values are used directly.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Sum all polygon areas to get \(A_{total}\).
  2. Compute \(P_i \times A_i\) for each gauge and sum them.
  3. Divide by \(A_{total}\) to get \(\bar{P}\).

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q49
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: The infiltration rate \( f \) in a basin under ponding condition is given by \( f = 30 + 10e^{-2t} \), where, \( f \) is in mm/h and \( t \) is time in hour. Total depth of infiltration (in mm, up to one decimal place) during the last 20 minutes of a storm of 30 minutes duration is _______
questions.explanation:
Hydrology | Infiltration

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Horton's infiltration equation: \(f = 30 + 10e^{-2t}\) (\(f\) in mm/h, \(t\) in hours)
    • Storm duration: 30 minutes
  • Aim: Find the total depth of infiltration (mm) during the last 20 minutes of the storm.

3. Core Concepts:

To find total infiltration depth over a time window, integrate the rate equation:

\[F = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} f(t)\, dt \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Convert all times to hours (since \(t\) in the equation is in hours).
  2. The last 20 minutes of a 30-minute storm = interval from \(t_1 = 10 \text{ min} = 1/6 \text{ h}\) to \(t_2 = 30 \text{ min} = 1/2 \text{ h}\).
  3. Set up and evaluate the definite integral analytically.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Setup the Integral\[F = \int_{1/6}^{1/2} (30 + 10e^{-2t})\, dt \]
  2. Step 2: Integrate\[ F = \left[30t - 5e^{-2t} \right]_{1/6}^{1/2} \]
  3. Step 3: Evaluate Upper Limit (\(t = 1/2\))\[F_{upper} = 30\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) - 5e^{-1} = 15 - \dfrac{5}{2.7183} = 15 - 1.8394 = 13.1606 \text{ mm} \]
  4. Step 4: Evaluate Lower Limit (\(t = 1/6\))\[F_{lower} = 30\left(\dfrac{1}{6}\right) - 5e^{-1/3} = 5 - 5(0.7165) = 5 - 3.5826 = 1.4174 \text{ mm} \]
  5. Step 5: Total Depth\[F = 13.1606 - 1.4174 = 11.7432 \approx 11.7 \text{ mm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 11.7 mm | Accepted key range: 11.0 to 12.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q50
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: In a laboratory, a flow experiment is performed over a hydraulic structure. The measured values of discharge and velocity are 0.05 m³/s and 0.25 m/s, respectively. If the full scale structure (30 times bigger) is subjected to a discharge of 270 m³/s, then the time scale (model to full scale) value (up to two decimal places) is _______
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Dimensional Analysis & Model Studies

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Model Discharge: \(Q_m = 0.05 \text{ m}^3/\text{s}\)
    • Model Velocity: \(v_m = 0.25 \text{ m/s}\)
    • Scale Ratio: \(L_r = L_m / L_p = 1/30\)
    • Prototype Discharge: \(Q_p = 270 \text{ m}^3/\text{s}\)
  • Aim: Find the time scale ratio \(T_r = T_m / T_p\).

3. Core Concepts:

The dimensions of discharge are \([Q] = L^3 T^{-1}\), so:

\[Q_r = \dfrac{L_r^3}{T_r} \implies T_r = \dfrac{L_r^3}{Q_r} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Find the discharge ratio \(Q_r = Q_m / Q_p\).
  2. Use the kinematic relationship to isolate \(T_r\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Discharge Scale Ratio\[Q_r = \dfrac{Q_m}{Q_p} = \dfrac{0.05}{270} = \dfrac{1}{5400} \]
  2. Step 2: Time Scale Ratio\[T_r = \dfrac{L_r^3}{Q_r} = \dfrac{(1/30)^3}{1/5400} = \dfrac{1/27{,}000}{1/5400} = \dfrac{5400}{27{,}000} = \dfrac{1}{5} = 0.20 \]

Sanity Check via Velocity: If \(T_r = 0.2\), then \(V_r = L_r / T_r = (1/30)/(1/5) = 1/6\). Given \(v_m = 0.25 \text{ m/s}\), prototype velocity \(v_p = 0.25 \times 6 = 1.5 \text{ m/s}\). Then \(Q_p = 900 \times A_m \times 1.5 = 1350 \times (0.05/0.25) = 270 \text{ m}^3/\text{s}\). ✓

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.20 | Accepted key range: 0.15 to 0.25

questions.question:
A water sample analysis data is given below.

IonConcentration, mg/LAtomic Weight
Ca²⁺6040

HCO₃⁻40061


The carbonate hardness (expressed as mg/L of CaCO₃, up to one decimal place) for the water sample is _______
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Water Quality

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) = 60 mg/L, Atomic Weight = 40
    • \(\text{Mg}^{2+}\) = 30 mg/L, Atomic Weight = 24.31
    • \(\text{HCO}_3^-\) = 400 mg/L, Molecular Weight = 61
  • Aim: Calculate Carbonate Hardness (CH) in mg/L as \(\text{CaCO}_3\), to one decimal place.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Total Hardness (TH): Sum of multivalent cations converted to equivalent \(\text{CaCO}_3\).
  • Total Alkalinity (TA): Anions causing alkalinity converted to equivalent \(\text{CaCO}_3\).
  • Carbonate Hardness: \(\text{CH} = \min(\text{TH},\ \text{TA})\)
  • Equivalent Weight: \(\text{Eq. Wt.} = \dfrac{\text{Molecular Weight}}{\text{Valency}}\)
    • \(\text{CaCO}_3\): Eq. Wt. \(= 100/2 = 50\)
    • \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\): Eq. Wt. \(= 40/2 = 20\)
    • \(\text{Mg}^{2+}\): Eq. Wt. \(= 24.31/2 = 12.155\)
    • \(\text{HCO}_3^-\): Eq. Wt. \(= 61/1 = 61\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Convert all concentrations to mg/L as \(\text{CaCO}_3\).
  2. Apply \(\text{CH} = \min(\text{TH}, \text{TA})\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Total Hardness (TH)\[\text{TH} = 60 \times \dfrac{50}{20} + 30 \times \dfrac{50}{12.155} \]\[\text{TH} = 60 \times 2.5 + 30 \times 4.1135 = 150 + 123.405 = 273.405 \text{ mg/L as CaCO}_3 \]
  2. Step 2: Total Alkalinity (TA)\[\text{TA} = 400 \times \dfrac{50}{61} = 400 \times 0.81967 = 327.868 \text{ mg/L as CaCO}_3 \]
  3. Step 3: Carbonate Hardness
    Since \(\text{TH} (273.405) < \text{TA} (327.868)\):\[\text{CH} = \text{TH} = 273.4 \text{ mg/L as CaCO}_3 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 273.4 mg/L | Accepted key range: 272.0 to 274.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q52
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: The ultimate BOD (\( L_0 \)) of a wastewater sample is estimated as 87% of COD. The COD of this wastewater is 300 mg/L. Considering first order BOD reaction rate constant k (use natural log) = 0.23 per day and temperature coefficient θ = 1.047, the BOD value (in mg/L, up to one decimal place) after three days of incubation at 27°C for this wastewater will be _______
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Characteristics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Ultimate BOD: \(L_0 = 87\%\) of COD
    • COD = 300 mg/L
    • BOD rate constant at 20°C: \(k_{20} = 0.23 \text{ day}^{-1}\) (base \(e\))
    • Temperature coefficient: \(\theta = 1.047\)
    • Incubation time: \(t = 3\) days at \(T = 27^\circ\text{C}\)
  • Aim: Calculate BOD exerted (\(y_t\)) in mg/L after 3 days at 27°C.

3. Core Concepts:

BOD Kinetics:

\[y_t = L_0(1 - e^{-kt}) \]

Temperature Correction (Arrhenius):

\[k_T = k_{20} \cdot \theta^{(T-20)} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine \(L_0\).
  2. Adjust \(k\) from 20°C to 27°C using \(\theta\).
  3. Calculate the 3-day BOD using \(k_{27}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Ultimate BOD\[L_0 = 0.87 \times 300 = 261 \text{ mg/L} \]
  2. Step 2: Temperature-Corrected Rate Constant\[k_{27} = 0.23 \times (1.047)^{(27-20)} = 0.23 \times (1.047)^7 = 0.23 \times 1.3796 = 0.31731 \text{ day}^{-1} \]
  3. Step 3: BOD at 3 Days\[y_3 = 261 \times (1 - e^{-0.31731 \times 3}) = 261 \times (1 - e^{-0.95193}) \]\[y_3 = 261 \times (1 - 0.3860) = 261 \times 0.6140 = 160.25 \text{ mg/L} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 160.2 mg/L | Accepted key range: 154.0 to 161.0

A waste activated sludge (WAS) is to be blended with green waste (GW). The carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) contents, per kg of WAS and GW, on dry basis are given in the table.

ParameterWASGW

The ratio of WAS to GW required (up to two decimal places) to achieve a blended C:N ratio of 20:1 on dry basis is _______

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    ComponentCarbon (g/kg)Nitrogen (g/kg)
    Waste Activated Sludge (WAS)5410
    Green Waste (GW)3606
  • Target blended C:N ratio = 20:1
  • Aim: Find the blending mass ratio \(R = M_{WAS} / M_{GW}\).

3. Core Concepts:

By conservation of mass, total carbon and nitrogen in the blend are sums from each component:

\[\dfrac{C_{blend}}{N_{blend}} = \dfrac{M_{WAS} \cdot C_{WAS} + M_{GW} \cdot C_{GW}}{M_{WAS} \cdot N_{WAS} + M_{GW} \cdot N_{GW}} \]

Dividing numerator and denominator by \(M_{GW}\) gives a direct equation in \(R\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Substitute \(R = M_{WAS}/M_{GW}\) and set the blend ratio equal to 20.
  2. Solve the resulting linear equation for \(R\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Setup Mass Balance\[\dfrac{54R + 360}{10R + 6} = 20 \]
  2. Step 2: Solve for \(R\)\[54R + 360 = 20(10R + 6) \]\[54R + 360 = 200R + 120 \]\[240 = 146R \]\[R = \dfrac{240}{146} = 1.6438 \approx 1.64 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.64 | Accepted key range: 1.60 to 1.70

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q54
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question: Given the following data: design life \( n = 15 \) years, lane distribution factor \( D = 0.75 \), annual rate of growth of commercial vehicles \( r = 6\% \), vehicle damage factor \( F = 4 \) and initial traffic in the year of completion of construction = 3000 Commercial Vehicles Per Day (CVPD). As per IRC:37-2012, the design traffic in terms of cumulative number of standard axles (in million standard axles, up to two decimal places) is _______
questions.explanation:
Transportation Engineering | Pavement Design

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Design life: \(n = 15 \text{ years}\)
    • Lane distribution factor: \(D = 0.75\)
    • Annual growth rate: \(r = 6\% = 0.06\)
    • Vehicle damage factor: \(F = 4\)
    • Initial traffic in year of completion: \(A = 3000 \text{ CVPD}\)
  • Aim: Compute cumulative standard axles (\(N\)) in million standard axles (msa) per IRC:37-2012.

3. Core Concepts:

IRC:37-2012 Formula:

\[ N = \dfrac{365 \times A \times [(1+r)^n - 1]}{r} \times D \times F \]

where \(A\) = initial traffic (CVPD) in year of completion, \(r\) = annual growth rate (decimal), \(n\) = design life (years), \(D\) = lane distribution factor, \(F\) = vehicle damage factor.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the compound growth multiplier \(\dfrac{(1+r)^n - 1}{r}\).
  2. Substitute all values into the IRC formula.
  3. Convert the result to million standard axles (msa).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Growth Multiplier\[(1.06)^{15} = 2.396558 \]\[\text{Multiplier} = \dfrac{2.396558 - 1}{0.06} = \dfrac{1.396558}{0.06} = 23.276 \]
  2. Step 2: Apply IRC Formula\[N = 365 \times 3000 \times 23.276 \times 0.75 \times 4 \]\[N = 1{,}095{,}000 \times 23.276 \times 3 = 76{,}461{,}561 \text{ standard axles} \]
  3. Step 3: Convert to msa\[N_{msa} = \dfrac{76{,}461{,}561}{10^6} \approx 76.46 \text{ msa} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 76.46 msa | Accepted key range: 75.00 to 78.00

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q55
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question: An aircraft approaches the threshold of a runway strip at a speed of 200 km/h. The pilot decelerates the aircraft at a rate of 1.697 m/s² and takes 18 s to exit the runway strip. If the deceleration after exiting the runway is 1 m/s², then the distance (in m, up to one decimal place) of the gate position from the location of exit on the runway is _______
questions.explanation:
Transportation Engineering | Airport Engineering

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Approach speed: \(V_1 = 200 \text{ km/h}\)
    • Deceleration on runway: \(a_1 = -1.697 \text{ m/s}^2\)
    • Time on runway before exit: \(t_1 = 18 \text{ s}\)
    • Deceleration on taxiway: \(a_2 = -1 \text{ m/s}^2\)
    • Final speed at gate: \(V_3 = 0 \text{ m/s}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the distance from runway exit to the gate (\(D_2\)) in meters.

3. Core Concepts:

This is a sequential 1D linear kinematics problem.

  • Velocity-Time: \(v = u + at\) — to find speed at exit
  • Velocity-Displacement: \(v^2 - u^2 = 2as\) — to find stopping distance on taxiway
  • Unit conversion: \(1 \text{ km/h} = \dfrac{5}{18} \text{ m/s}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Convert \(V_1\) from km/h to m/s.
  2. Calculate exit speed \(V_2\) using runway kinematics.
  3. Use \(V_2\) as initial speed for taxiway phase; solve for \(D_2\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Convert Approach Speed\[V_1 = 200 \times \dfrac{5}{18} = 55.556 \text{ m/s} \]
  2. Step 2: Speed at Runway Exit (\(V_2\))\[V_2 = V_1 + a_1 t_1 = 55.556 + (-1.697 \times 18) = 55.556 - 30.546 = 25.010 \text{ m/s} \]
  3. Step 3: Taxiway Distance (\(D_2\))\[V_3^2 - V_2^2 = 2a_2 D_2 \]\[0 - (25.010)^2 = 2(-1)D_2 \]\[D_2 = \dfrac{625.48}{2} = 312.74 \text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 312.7 m | Accepted key range: 311.0 to 319.0
